theory_content: Gross rental yield is annual rent divided by the purchase price. In most Indian cities it runs 2-4%. Against a home loan at 8.5%, a 3% yield means the property costs you 5.5% a year to hold before maintenance, property tax and vacancy. A rental that yields less than the loan rate is a bet on price appreciation alone.

theory_title: The 8-10% you pay to change your mind
theory_content: Stamp duty, registration, brokerage and legal fees typically total 8-10% of the price, and selling costs more on top. This is why the rent-versus-buy calculation turns on how long you will stay: below about seven years the transaction costs usually exceed any appreciation.

theory_title: The risk that only shows up when you need out
theory_content: A flat cannot be sold in a day, cannot be sold in parts, and in a weak market may not sell for months at any price you would accept. Equity can be liquidated in a session. Property concentration is therefore two risks at once: a single asset, in a single city, that you cannot exit quickly.

A Real Estate Investment Trust holds commercial property and must distribute at least 90% of its income. Units trade on the exchange, so they are liquid and divisible, and the minimum investment is a few thousand rupees rather than a few crore. The distributions are taxed in parts at different rates, which is the main complication.
